--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add multiple edges to the graph in a single call. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add multiple edges to the graph in a single call. title: >- [Graph.add_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Add multiple edges to the graph in a single call. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add multiple edges to the graph in a single call. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1959-L2177){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_edges( edges, rel=None, weight=None, auto_create_nodes=False, **shared_attrs, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Add several edges](../assets/graphs/add-edges.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: four nodes with two edges, B to A to C. After: two new edges, B to D and C to D, appear in the accent color in one call and close the cycle; no nodes are added." width="100%"} A bulk version of `add_edge()` that accepts a list of `(source, target)` pairs and applies shared attributes to all of them. A third element sets that edge's weight (a number) or overrides the shared attributes (a dict), so a weighted edge list reads like NetworkX's `add_weighted_edges_from()`: `[("A", "B", 2.0), ("B", "C", 0.5)]`. Endpoints are resolved exactly as in `add_edge()`: integers are node IDs and strings are node labels. Edges are added in list order, each with its own auto-assigned edge ID, and repeated pairs create parallel edges. The whole call is recorded as a single step in the step log (see `steps`). Typical uses: - wiring up a node set created with `add_nodes()` - building a graph directly from an edge list with `auto_create_nodes=True` - tagging a batch of edges with a common `rel=`, `weight=` or other attribute Every item's shape is checked before any edge is added, so a malformed item leaves the graph unchanged. Endpoints are only resolved while adding, though: if one can't be resolved part-way through the list, the edges before it have already been added when the error is raised. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Edge definitions to add. Each element can be: - `(source, target)`: shared attributes and `weight=` apply. - `(source, target, weight)`: a number (int, float or NumPy scalar) that sets this edge's weight, overriding `weight=`. - `(source, target, attrs_dict)`: the dict is merged on top of `**shared_attrs=` and may also contain `"rel"` and `"weight"` keys to override `rel=` and `weight=` for that edge. - `(source, target, weight, attrs_dict)`: both of the above. The dict must not also contain `"weight"`. Lists work in place of tuples. Any other shape (a bare string, a non-numeric, non-dict third element, or a different length) raises an error rather than being silently truncated. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional relationship type applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). Stored in the first-class `rel` column of the edge DataFrame. Default is `None`. [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional numeric weight applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). As with `add_edge()`, the value is stored whether or not the graph was created with `weighted=True`. Default is `None` (no weight). [auto_create_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, automatically create nodes for string labels that don't exist yet (integer IDs are never auto-created). If `False` (default), all referenced nodes must already exist. [**shared_attrs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Attributes applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge), e.g., `color="gray"`. Each key becomes a column in the edge DataFrame. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an item isn't one of the accepted shapes (checked before any edge is added). [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an item gives its weight both as the third element and in its dict, or if a source or target can't be resolved to an existing node (and `auto_create_nodes=` is `False`). ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~add_edge`) : Add one edge. [](`~add_edges_by_id`) : Add edges between node IDs. [](`~from_edges`) : Build a new graph from an edge list. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Add several edges at once between existing nodes: ::: {#4c661392 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: A number as the third element is that edge's weight, which makes weighted edge lists compact: ::: {#879a36ed .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(weighted=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", 2.0), ("B", "C", 0.5), ("A", "C", 3.0)]) ) graph.get_edge_df().select(["source", "target", "weight"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: A dict as the third tuple element overrides the shared values for that edge only. Here the A-C edge gets its own weight and `rel`, while A-B keeps the shared ones: ::: {#d717499e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("A", "C", {"weight": 2.0, "rel": "strong"}), ], rel="weak", weight=1.0, ) ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: With `auto_create_nodes=True`, a graph can be built straight from an edge list. The three people are created as nodes on the fly: ::: {#8c326fac .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_edges( [("Alice", "Bob"), ("Bob", "Carol"), ("Carol", "Alice")], rel="knows", auto_create_nodes=True, ) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` (3, 3) ``` ::: ::: ### Payments in batches A bank's payments arrive in batches, and a shared `rel=` tags each batch with what it was for: the payroll, the rent and the card payments. Every edge in a batch gets the same `rel`, while its amount is its own: ::: {#58ff977b .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} bank = ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) bank.add_edges( [("Acme", "Dee", 2600), ("Acme", "Eve", 2700), ("Acme", "Max", 2400)], rel="wages", auto_create_nodes=True, ) bank.add_edges( [("Max", "Landlord", 1800)], rel="rent", auto_create_nodes=True ) bank.add_edges( [ ("Dee", "Grocer", 64), ("Eve", "Grocer", 38), ("Max", "Grocer", 82), ("Dee", "Cafe", 12), ("Eve", "Cafe", 15), ], rel="card", auto_create_nodes=True, ) bank.plot( edge_color_by="rel", edge_width_by="weight", label_by="label", seed=1 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The wages flow out of Acme and the card payments into the Grocer and the Cafe, and the rent is the one large payment that doesn't come from Acme.
